title: 1 Samuel Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 28.

questions.question: Who told David that he would go out with him to battle along with his men?
options: Achish
Saul
Samuel
The Philistine king
questions.correctAnswer: Achish
questions.explanation: Achish said unto David, Know thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men (1 Samuel 28:1).

questions.question: What position did Achish promise to give David forever?
options: Keeper of his head
Captain of his army
Chief advisor
Priest of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Keeper of his head
questions.explanation: Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee keeper of mine head for ever (1 Samuel 28:2).

questions.question: Where was Samuel buried after he died?
options: Ramah
Gilboa
Endor
Shunem
questions.correctAnswer: Ramah
questions.explanation: Samuel was buried in Ramah, even in his own city (1 Samuel 28:3).

questions.question: What did Saul do to those that had familiar spirits and wizards in the land?
options: Put them away
Made them his advisors
Protected them
Ignored them
questions.correctAnswer: Put them away
questions.explanation: Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land (1 Samuel 28:3).

questions.question: Where did the Philistines pitch their camp?
options: Shunem
Gilboa
Ramah
Endor
questions.correctAnswer: Shunem
questions.explanation: The Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem (1 Samuel 28:4).

questions.question: What was Saul's reaction when he saw the host of the Philistines?
options: He was afraid and his heart greatly trembled
He was confident and joyful
He ignored them
He immediately attacked
questions.correctAnswer: He was afraid and his heart greatly trembled
questions.explanation: When Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled (1 Samuel 28:5).

questions.question: Did the LORD answer Saul when he enquired of Him by dreams, Urim, or prophets?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets (1 Samuel 28:6).

questions.question: What did Saul command his servants to find for him?
options: A woman that hath a familiar spirit
A mighty warrior
A wise prophet
A skilled blacksmith
questions.correctAnswer: A woman that hath a familiar spirit
questions.explanation: Saul said to his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her (1 Samuel 28:7).

questions.question: Where was the woman with a familiar spirit located?
options: Endor
Gilboa
Ramah
Shunem
questions.correctAnswer: Endor
questions.explanation: His servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit at Endor (1 Samuel 28:7).

questions.question: How did Saul prepare himself before going to the woman with a familiar spirit?
options: He disguised himself and put on other raiment
He prayed in the temple
He gathered many men
He fasted for three days
questions.correctAnswer: He disguised himself and put on other raiment
questions.explanation: Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him (1 Samuel 28:8).

questions.question: What did Saul ask the woman to do when he came to her?
options: Divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up whom I shall name
Prepare a meal for me
Tell me the future without spirits
Hide me from the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up whom I shall name
questions.explanation: Saul said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee (1 Samuel 28:8).

questions.question: True or False: The woman was afraid to help Saul because she knew he had cut off those that had familiar spirits and wizards out of the land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The woman said to Saul, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land (1 Samuel 28:9).

questions.question: What did Saul swear to the woman to persuade her to help him?
options: That no punishment shall happen to her for this thing
That he would pay her handsomely
That he would protect her from the king
That she would become queen
questions.correctAnswer: That no punishment shall happen to her for this thing
questions.explanation: Saul sware to her by the LORD, saying, As the LORD liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing (1 Samuel 28:10).

questions.question: True or False: The woman immediately knew it was Saul when he came to her.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The woman saw Samuel and cried out, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul (1 Samuel 28:12).

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 28, which event happened first?
options: Saul sought a woman with a familiar spirit
The Philistines pitched at Shunem
Samuel died and was buried in Ramah
Saul enquired of the LORD but received no answer
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel died and was buried in Ramah
questions.explanation: Samuel's death and burial in Ramah is mentioned before the Philistines pitched at Shunem and Saul's enquiries (1 Samuel 28:3).

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Saul swear to the woman with a familiar spirit regarding her safety?
options: No punishment shall happen to her for this thing
He would reward her richly
He would keep her secret forever
He would protect her family
questions.correctAnswer: No punishment shall happen to her for this thing
questions.explanation: Saul swore by the LORD that no punishment would happen to the woman for her actions, as stated in 1 Samuel 28:10.

questions.question: Whom did Saul ask the woman to bring up by the familiar spirit?
options: Samuel
David
Goliath
Jonathan
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel
questions.explanation: Saul specifically requested the woman to bring up Samuel, as he wanted guidance from the deceased prophet, stated in 1 Samuel 28:11.

questions.question: How did the woman react when she saw Samuel appear?
options: She cried out loudly and questioned Saul
She fainted and fell to the ground
She rejoiced and praised God
She immediately fled the house
questions.correctAnswer: She cried out loudly and questioned Saul
questions.explanation: The woman cried with a loud voice and questioned Saul why he had deceived her by coming himself, as shown in 1 Samuel 28:12.

questions.question: What did the woman say she saw as Saul asked her not to be afraid?
options: Gods ascending out of the earth
Angels descending from heaven
Fire and smoke
A vision of the future
questions.correctAnswer: Gods ascending out of the earth
questions.explanation: The woman told Saul that she saw gods ascending out of the earth, as recorded in 1 Samuel 28:13.

questions.question: What form did the woman describe Samuel to be when he appeared?
options: An old man covered with a mantle
A young warrior with a sword
A shining angel in white robes
A child with a harp
questions.correctAnswer: An old man covered with a mantle
questions.explanation: The woman described Samuel's form as an old man covered with a mantle, leading Saul to recognize him, according to 1 Samuel 28:14.

questions.question: Why did Saul say he had called up Samuel from the dead?
options: Because he was sore distressed and God did not answer him
Because he wanted to prove his power to the people
Because he sought to curse David
Because he desired to hear a prophecy about the future
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was sore distressed and God did not answer him
questions.explanation: Saul said he was sore distressed because of the Philistine war and that God no longer answered him through prophets or dreams, so he called Samuel for guidance, as explained in 1 Samuel 28:15.

questions.question: What reason did Samuel give for the LORD having departed from Saul and become his enemy?
options: Because Saul disobeyed the voice of the LORD and did not execute His fierce wrath upon Amalek
Because Saul worshipped other gods
Because Saul sought guidance from a familiar spirit
Because Saul failed to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul disobeyed the voice of the LORD and did not execute His fierce wrath upon Amalek
questions.explanation: Samuel explained that the LORD departed from Saul because he disobeyed God's command and did not carry out His fierce wrath on Amalek, as stated in 1 Samuel 28:18.

questions.question: According to Samuel, what will happen to Saul and his sons the next day?
options: They will be with Samuel in death
They will defeat the Philistines
They will be crowned as kings
They will escape safely
questions.correctAnswer: They will be with Samuel in death
questions.explanation: Samuel foretold that Saul and his sons would die the next day and be with him, indicating their impending death, as recorded in 1 Samuel 28:19.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience can we learn from Saul’s experience in this chapter?
options: Disobedience to God leads to loss of favor and dire consequences
Seeking guidance from others is better than trusting God
Fear is a sign of weak faith and should be ignored
Disguising oneself is a wise strategy in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience to God leads to loss of favor and dire consequences
questions.explanation: Saul’s disobedience caused God to depart from him and led to his downfall, teaching that faith and obedience are essential, as shown in 1 Samuel 28:16-18.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 28:18-19 connect disobedience to the consequences Saul faces?
options: Because Saul disobeyed God’s command, the LORD has delivered Israel into the Philistines’ hand and Saul will die
Because Saul obeyed partially, he will be spared but Israel will suffer
Because Saul sought counsel from the familiar spirit, he will be forgiven
Because Saul prayed earnestly, God will reverse his judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul disobeyed God’s command, the LORD has delivered Israel into the Philistines’ hand and Saul will die
questions.explanation: The passage connects Saul’s disobedience to God’s judgment—Israel will be defeated, and Saul and his sons will die, as explained in 1 Samuel 28:18-19.

questions.question: What does Saul’s refusal to eat after speaking with Samuel teach about his state of mind?
options: He was deeply troubled and fearful, lacking strength
He was confident and calm
He was indifferent to his fate
He was rejoicing in the prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: He was deeply troubled and fearful, lacking strength
questions.explanation: Saul was sore afraid and had no strength because he had eaten no bread all day and night, showing his deep distress, as noted in 1 Samuel 28:20.

questions.question: True or False: Saul’s servants and the woman compelled him to eat after he initially refused.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Though Saul initially refused to eat, his servants and the woman compelled him to eat so he might have strength, as stated in 1 Samuel 28:23.

questions.question: True or False: Saul’s consultation with the woman at Endor was approved by God as a righteous act.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The consultation was an act of desperation after God had departed from Saul; Samuel rebuked Saul, indicating it was not approved, as seen in 1 Samuel 28:16-17.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 28:14-15 reveal about Saul’s reaction to seeing Samuel and his state of heart?
options: Saul humbled himself and sought guidance because he was distressed and felt abandoned by God
Saul was angry and demanded answers aggressively
Saul laughed and dismissed the vision
Saul ignored Samuel’s words and left quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Saul humbled himself and sought guidance because he was distressed and felt abandoned by God
questions.explanation: Saul bowed himself upon seeing Samuel and expressed his distress over God’s silence, showing humility and desperation, as recorded in 1 Samuel 28:14-15.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD had already decided to give the kingdom to David before Saul consulted the woman at Endor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Samuel revealed that the LORD had already rent the kingdom from Saul and given it to David, showing God's prior judgment, as in 1 Samuel 28:17.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 28.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 28:19, what did the LORD declare would happen to Saul and his sons the next day?
options: They would triumph over the Philistines
They would be with Samuel in death
They would escape and flee to the mountains
They would be made kings over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They would be with Samuel in death
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:19 states that Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day, indicating their imminent death in battle.

questions.question: Why did Saul fall down on the earth and become very afraid according to 1 Samuel 28:20?
options: Because he saw a vision of the Lord
Because of the words of Samuel
Because he was attacked by the Philistines
Because he realized David would become king
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the words of Samuel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:20 explains that Saul fell down and was very afraid due to the message Samuel gave him through the medium.

questions.question: What did the woman who had a familiar spirit say to Saul after seeing Samuel in 1 Samuel 28:21?
options: She warned him of his defeat
She said she had obeyed Saul's voice and risked her life
She told him to flee the battle
She asked him to leave her house
questions.correctAnswer: She said she had obeyed Saul's voice and risked her life
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:21 records the woman's statement that she obeyed Saul's voice and put her life in danger by consulting the familiar spirit for him.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 28:22, what did the woman request Saul to do to gain strength?
options: Drink water
Rest on the bed
Eat a morsel of bread
Pray for deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Eat a morsel of bread
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:22 shows the woman asking Saul to eat bread to regain strength as he prepared to go on his way.

questions.question: How did Saul initially respond to the woman's offer of bread in 1 Samuel 28:23?
options: He eagerly accepted
He refused to eat
He asked for wine instead
He demanded more food
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to eat
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 28:23, Saul refused the bread at first, but was eventually persuaded by his servants and the woman to eat.

questions.question: What did the woman do to prepare food for Saul and his servants as described in 1 Samuel 28:24?
options: She slaughtered a fat calf and baked unleavened bread
She cooked fish and barley
She prepared roasted lamb and wine
She offered bread and honey
questions.correctAnswer: She slaughtered a fat calf and baked unleavened bread
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:24 reports that the woman killed a fat calf and baked unleavened bread for Saul and his servants.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 1 Samuel 28:15-19 to highlight Saul's tragic fate?
options: Chiasmus
Parable
Allegory
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The passage from 1 Samuel 28:15-19 uses chiasmus, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to emphasize Saul's disobedience and the consequences foretold by Samuel.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'familiar spirit' (used in 1 Samuel 28:7) imply in the context of this chapter?
options: A spirit of prophecy from God
A necromancer or medium who communicates with the dead
An angelic messenger
A demon of deception
questions.correctAnswer: A necromancer or medium who communicates with the dead
questions.explanation: The term 'familiar spirit' in 1 Samuel 28:7 refers to a medium or necromancer who purportedly communicates with the dead, which was forbidden in Israelite law.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of Saul's rejection by God due to disobedience, as seen in 1 Samuel 28:17-18?
options: Deuteronomy 17:14-20
1 Samuel 15:22-23
Psalm 23
Isaiah 53
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 15:22-23
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:22-23 deals with Saul’s disobedience and God’s rejection of him as king, which is echoed in 1 Samuel 28:17-18 where Samuel reminds Saul of his failure to obey God's command.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 28:6 demonstrate the failure of traditional means of divine communication for Saul?
options: God answered Saul through a dream
God answered through prophets only
God did not answer Saul by dreams, Urim, or prophets
God spoke directly to Saul
questions.correctAnswer: God did not answer Saul by dreams, Urim, or prophets
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:6 clearly states that the LORD did not answer Saul by any of the usual methods, including dreams, the Urim, or prophets, prompting Saul to seek a medium.

questions.question: What historical-cultural significance does Saul’s visit to the woman at Endor (1 Samuel 28:7-8) have in the context of ancient Israelite society?
options: It was a common and accepted practice
It represented desperation and violation of the Mosaic law
It was a royal ritual for kings
It was a prophetic ceremony
questions.correctAnswer: It represented desperation and violation of the Mosaic law
questions.explanation: In Israelite culture, consulting mediums was forbidden (Leviticus 19:31); Saul’s visit (1 Samuel 28:7-8) shows his desperation and disobedience to God's commands.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's kingdom being taken away from one and given to another, as in 1 Samuel 28:17?
options: Matthew 21:43
Acts 2:38
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 21:43
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:43 speaks of the kingdom of God being taken from one and given to another, paralleling the theme of 1 Samuel 28:17 where the kingdom is taken from Saul and given to David.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 28:16, what is the relationship between the LORD and Saul at this point?
options: The LORD is forgiving Saul
The LORD is Saul's ally
The LORD has departed from Saul and become his enemy
The LORD is silent towards Saul
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD has departed from Saul and become his enemy
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:16 explicitly states that the LORD has departed from Saul and become his enemy, highlighting the severity of Saul’s rejection.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 28:25, Saul and his servants ate the food prepared by the woman before departing that night.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:25 confirms that Saul and his servants ate the food brought by the woman before they left that night.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel was alive and directly spoke to Saul in 1 Samuel 28.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:3 states that Samuel was dead and had been buried; the figure Saul spoke to was a spirit summoned by the medium, not the living Samuel.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the significance of Saul's inability to receive an answer from the LORD by dreams, Urim, or prophets as described in this chapter?
options: It shows God’s judgment and withdrawal of guidance from Saul
It indicates that God was silent because Saul was righteous
It reveals that Saul had spiritual insight independent of God
It means the LORD was testing Saul’s faith
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s judgment and withdrawal of guidance from Saul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:6 explains that Saul enquired of the LORD but received no answer, indicating God had withdrawn His guidance due to Saul's disobedience, demonstrating divine judgment. This aligns with Deuteronomy 28:20, where God’s disfavor results in lack of prophetic guidance.

questions.question: How does Saul’s action of seeking a woman with a familiar spirit reflect on the doctrine of sanctification and divine law?
options: It demonstrates Saul’s continued disobedience to God’s command against necromancy
It shows Saul’s adherence to God’s law by seeking divine counsel
It indicates that Saul was sanctified and protected by God
It reveals that Saul was testing the power of familiar spirits
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates Saul’s continued disobedience to God’s command against necromancy
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:7 shows Saul seeking a woman with a familiar spirit despite having expelled such persons earlier, highlighting his disobedience and failure to sanctify himself according to God’s law (Leviticus 19:31).

questions.question: What does the appearance of Samuel’s spirit to Saul reveal about the reality of the afterlife and God’s sovereign control over death and revelation?
options: It confirms that God allows revelation from the dead only by His permission
It suggests that the dead can independently communicate with the living
It indicates the futility of seeking the dead for guidance
It shows that familiar spirits have real power apart from God
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms that God allows revelation from the dead only by His permission
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 28:11-15, Samuel’s spirit appears by divine allowance, emphasizing God’s sovereignty over life, death, and revelation, consistent with Hebrews 9:27 where men die once and face judgment.

questions.question: According to Samuel’s message to Saul, what doctrinal truth is revealed about God’s justice and covenant faithfulness?
options: God’s justice involves punishment for persistent disobedience
God’s covenant faithfulness guarantees Saul’s kingdom forever
God’s justice is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions
God forgives Saul unconditionally despite his sins
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice involves punishment for persistent disobedience
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:16-18 reveals that because Saul disobeyed God, His justice entails the removal of Saul’s kingdom, demonstrating that God's covenant faithfulness coexists with righteous judgment (Psalm 89:30-34).

questions.question: How does Saul’s response to the prophecy of his death and defeat relate to the doctrine of human responsibility under divine sovereignty?
options: Saul’s fear and refusal to eat show his acknowledgment of divine sovereignty and his own responsibility
Saul’s response shows he blames God and denies responsibility
Saul’s reaction indicates he believes he can avoid the prophecy
Saul’s behavior shows he is indifferent to God’s judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Saul’s fear and refusal to eat show his acknowledgment of divine sovereignty and his own responsibility
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:20-23 records Saul’s fear and weakness, illustrating his recognition of God’s sovereign judgment and his personal accountability in facing it (Romans 14:12).

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by His refusal to answer Saul through traditional means in this chapter?
options: God’s holiness and justice in punishing sin
God’s omnipotence in controlling nature
God’s mercy in forgiving all sins
God’s omniscience in foretelling the future
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and justice in punishing sin
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:6 shows God’s refusal to answer Saul, reflecting His holiness that cannot tolerate disobedience and His justice in exacting consequences for sin (Habakkuk 1:13).

questions.question: How does the chapter illustrate the consequences of Saul’s failure to execute God’s wrath upon Amalek in terms of divine retribution?
options: God removed Saul’s kingdom as a direct result of his disobedience
God rewarded Saul despite his failure
God was indifferent to Saul’s actions against Amalek
God forgave Saul without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: God removed Saul’s kingdom as a direct result of his disobedience
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:18 explicitly connects Saul’s failure to obey God’s command against Amalek with the loss of his kingdom, demonstrating divine retribution (1 Samuel 15:23).

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing Saul’s fear upon seeing the Philistine army (verse 5) with his seeking forbidden counsel (verses 7-20)?
options: Fear without faith leads to disobedience and seeking sinful solutions
Fear is a sign of righteousness and trust in God
Saul’s fear is unrelated to his spiritual state
Seeking forbidden counsel is a sign of strength
questions.correctAnswer: Fear without faith leads to disobedience and seeking sinful solutions
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:5 shows Saul’s fear, and 28:7-20 shows that his fear without trust in God led him to seek a witch, illustrating how lack of faith results in sinful choices (Psalm 56:3).

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 28 teach about the limits of human attempts to control or circumvent God’s will through supernatural means?
options: Such attempts are futile and result in further judgment
They effectively alter God’s plans
They are endorsed by God for guidance
They bring peace and success
questions.correctAnswer: Such attempts are futile and result in further judgment
questions.explanation: Saul’s attempt to contact Samuel through a medium (28:7-25) fails to change God’s judgment but instead confirms his doom, showing human efforts to circumvent divine will are futile (Galatians 6:7).

questions.question: How does the mention of David as Saul’s neighbor to whom the kingdom would be given (verse 17) reveal God’s providential plan in redemptive history?
options: It shows God’s sovereign plan to establish David’s dynasty as part of His redemptive covenant
It indicates God’s abandonment of Israel
It suggests David seized power by force against God’s will
It reveals God’s rejection of all Israel’s kings
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s sovereign plan to establish David’s dynasty as part of His redemptive covenant
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:17 reveals God’s providence in removing Saul and establishing David’s line, which is central to the messianic promise fulfilled in Christ (2 Samuel 7:12-16).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Saul’s consultation of the medium shows the Bible endorses necromancy. What does 1 Samuel 28:7-25 actually teach about this practice?
options: The Bible presents necromancy as forbidden and illustrates its futility and consequences
The Bible condones necromancy as a legitimate practice
The Bible is neutral about necromancy
The Bible encourages seeking spirits for guidance
questions.correctAnswer: The Bible presents necromancy as forbidden and illustrates its futility and consequences
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:7-25 shows Saul’s desperate and forbidden attempt to contact the dead, which results in judgment and fear, indicating necromancy is condemned and ineffective (Leviticus 19:31).

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by the LORD's declaration that He has become Saul’s enemy (verse 16) due to Saul's disobedience?
options: God’s holiness demands separation from persistent sin
God remains a friend regardless of sin
God ignores human rebellion
God’s love overrides all disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands separation from persistent sin
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:16 reveals that God has departed and become Saul’s enemy, illustrating that God’s holiness necessitates separation from unrepentant sin (Isaiah 59:2).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth is revealed by 1 Samuel 28:3 and 28:7 regarding the presence and prohibition of familiar spirits in Israel?
options: Israel was to be sanctified by removing all necromancy and forbidden spiritual practices
Familiar spirits were accepted and encouraged in Israel
The presence of familiar spirits was irrelevant to Israel’s covenant
Israel tolerated necromancy as cultural practice
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was to be sanctified by removing all necromancy and forbidden spiritual practices
questions.explanation: Verse 3 notes Samuel’s death and Saul’s expulsion of familiar spirits, while verse 7 shows Saul’s servants referencing a woman with such a spirit, emphasizing Israel’s call to holiness by rejecting necromancy (Leviticus 20:6).

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of Saul’s death prophecy and the rise of David in this chapter teach about God’s redemptive plan in salvation history?
options: God’s plan involves judgment of unfaithful leaders and the establishment of a Messianic line through David
God’s plan is unpredictable and lacks continuity
Saul’s dynasty is the ultimate fulfillment of God’s promise
God rejects all human kings without replacement
questions.correctAnswer: God’s plan involves judgment of unfaithful leaders and the establishment of a Messianic line through David
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:17-19 reveals the transfer of kingship to David, signifying God’s providential unfolding of redemption through David’s line culminating in Christ (Luke 1:32-33).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His allowing Samuel’s spirit to be summoned yet pronouncing judgment through him in this passage?
options: God’s sovereignty over spiritual realms and judgment
God’s weakness in permitting necromancy
God’s indifference to human sin
God’s endorsement of occult practices
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty over spiritual realms and judgment
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 28:11-15 shows God’s control over the spirit world by permitting Samuel’s appearance to deliver judgment, affirming His ultimate authority (Colossians 1:16).
